name: City of Brea Community Services Department (Brea Community Center)
orgTypeBasis: A municipal department of a single general-law city, not a branch of anything; its own page names three divisions it runs itself - Recreation Services, Arts and Human Services, and the Brea Community Center.
decisionMakerTitle: Recreation Services Manager, Community Services Department
whyTheyFit: The department works three divisions out of one building six-tenths of a mile from the venue and staffs the July 4th Country Fair and BreaFest in August with a seasonal bench it hires every spring, so its own thank-you falls in September when the summer programme ends - the week a new venue has the most weekday evening inventory and the fewest bookings.
buyingWindow: Sep (post-summer-programme staff thank-you), Nov-Dec (city holiday event)
headcountBasis: Three divisions plus a community centre carrying a front desk, KidWatch, a Teen Zone, meeting rooms and a rentals team implies a small full-time core over a large part-time recreation bench that peaks in summer; estimate only, the city publishes no departmental headcount.
note: Say this out loud: this department is a PROSPECT and a COMPETITOR at the same address. The Brea Community Center rents Community Hall for private parties, runs KidWatch and a Teen Zone, and sells youth recreation classes through BreaRec - every birthday and youth night it books is one the venue did not. Pitch the staff-appreciation side, and treat the recreation side as a referral trade (their overflow party enquiries) rather than a head-on fight.
addressSource: City of Brea facilities list at cityofbrea.gov/facilities, read 14 August 2026: the Art Studio and the Arts Garden, both listed on the city's own Brea Community Center facility page as rooms of that building, print 695 E. Madison Way, Brea, CA 92821.

name: City of Brea Human Resources Division
orgTypeBasis: A division of the City of Brea's administrative services, published on the city's own website with its own page and its own recruitment portal.
whyTheyFit: Brea is one of the few cities this size that still runs its own police department and its own fire department rather than contracting to the county, and this one third-floor division recruits and administers all of them, so the city-wide service awards and the all-employee holiday night are a single calendar owned by a single manager three-quarters of a mile from the venue rather than four departments buying separately.
buyingWindow: Nov-Dec (city-wide holiday event and service awards), early May (Public Service Recognition Week)
headcountBasis: A full-service city of roughly 48,000 running its own sworn police, its own fire department, community services and public works; full-time plus regular part-time. Estimate only - the city publishes budgeted positions in its adopted budget, which is the number to ask for on the first call.
note: No written door. The HR page publishes only a floor location inside the Brea Civic and Cultural Center and routes applicants to governmentjobs.com/careers/brea; the city's CivicPlus staff directory is closed to automated reading. Treat as a walk-in at the third-floor counter or a call to the city switchboard. The pin stacks with Brea Police Department and the OC Public Libraries Brea Branch, which share 1 Civic Center Cir - one visit reaches three separate payrolls.
addressSource: City of Brea Human Resources page (cityofbrea.gov/330/Human-Resources), read 14 August 2026, which places the division on the third floor of the Brea Civic and Cultural Center; the street address of that building, 1 Civic Center Circle, is printed on the city's own facilities list for the Brea Art Gallery, read the same day.

name: Brea Police Department
orgTypeBasis: A city-operated sworn police department - Brea has not contracted its policing out to the Sheriff, and the department posts its own recruitments under its own agency identifier.
decisionMakerTitle: Administrative Services Manager, Brea Police Department
whyTheyFit: A department that has to keep patrol on the street twenty-four hours cannot empty the building on a Friday night, so its recognition spend has to be bought as two or three smaller blocks timed around shift change - late morning and mid-afternoon midweek, which is the exact daypart a venue that has not opened yet has the hardest time selling.
buyingWindow: Mid-May (National Police Week), Dec (department holiday event), academy and field-training graduation dates
headcountBasis: Sworn officers plus dispatch, records and professional staff for a city of roughly 48,000 that runs its own department; estimate only, taken from the scale of the city rather than a published roster.
note: The verified address on file is a recruiting inbox, not a purchasing inbox - it was read off the department's own job posting on National Testing Network, which the agency authors. Use it to get a name, then ask for the Administrative Services Manager, who owns the department's non-sworn budget. Pin stacks with City of Brea Human Resources and the OC Public Libraries Brea Branch at 1 Civic Center Cir. THIS ADDRESS DECAYS. It was read off a National Testing Network recruitment posting dated 8 July 2026, and a job posting rolls off. Re-verify before any send; if the posting has gone, this row drops to a go-see rather than keeping a claim its source no longer supports.
addressSource: Brea Police Department job details published by the agency on National Testing Network, read 14 August 2026, printing 1 CIVIC CENTER CIRCLE BREA, CALIFORNIA 92821; the same street address appears on the City of Brea's own facilities list for the Brea Civic and Cultural Center.

name: Brea Firefighters Association
orgTypeBasis: A registered employee association and charitable entity separate from the city payroll - it is a Brea Chamber of Commerce member in its own name and runs its own public donation site at breafire.support4.org.
whyTheyFit: The association is the social and charitable arm of a fire department the city still runs itself, and it already raises money in public through a donation platform - which makes it the buyer for the crew-and-families night that cannot go on a city purchase order, and a natural counterparty for a fundraiser night where the venue takes the covers and the association takes the cause.
buyingWindow: Oct (Fire Prevention Month fundraising), Dec (crew and families holiday night)
headcountBasis: Membership tracks the sworn roster of a multi-station city fire department plus retirees; a families night multiplies the head count by roughly three. Estimate only - the association publishes no roster.
note: Two honest caveats. First, the chamber listing prints the ZIP as 92822, which is Brea's PO Box ZIP; the street itself geocodes in 92821 and the recorded address uses the street ZIP. Second, the only written door found is the chamber's own member contact form, not the association's - the association website publishes officer titles but no address, phone or email. Its street address is shared with Brea Fire administration, which the city's own pages give as One Civic Center Circle, (714) 990-7655.
addressSource: Brea Chamber of Commerce member directory listing for Brea Firefighters Association (business.breachamber.com), read 14 August 2026, printing 1 Civic Center Circle, Brea, CA, 92822; fire administration at One Civic Center Circle corroborated from the City of Brea's own station and apparatus page the same day.

name: City of La Habra Community Services Department (La Habra Community Center)
orgTypeBasis: One of the seven departments the City of La Habra names on its own government page, operating a single municipal community centre rather than a branch of a larger operator.
address: 101 W La Habra Blvd, La Habra, CA 90631
whyTheyFit: The department runs its whole recreation programme from one building on La Habra Boulevard and borrows the La Habra High School pool at 801 W. Highlander for its aquatics season, which means it hires and then releases a seasonal aquatics and camp staff on a fixed September date - a recurring end-of-season night, 2.8 miles from the venue, that repeats every year without anyone having to invent an occasion.
buyingWindow: Sep (end of aquatics and summer camp season), Nov-Dec (city holiday event)
headcountBasis: A single-centre recreation operation with a pool season implies a handful of full-time staff over a large summer part-time bench; estimate only, no published roster was reachable.
note: No written door was reachable: lahabraca.gov's CivicPlus staff directory, its Recreation form centre and its department contact pages all refused automated reading on 14 August 2026, so this is a counter visit rather than an email. The chamber listing names both a Recreation Manager and a Director, which is the two-name ladder to ask for at the desk. Prospect and competitor at once - the same building rents rooms and sells youth recreation, so lead with the staff-appreciation side.
addressSource: City of La Habra home page (lahabraca.gov), read 14 August 2026, which prints 101 W. La Habra Blvd. for the Community Center; corroborated by the La Habra Chamber of Commerce member listing for La Habra Community Center, read the same day, which also gives the phone.
matchedAddress: 101 W LA HABRA BLVD, LA HABRA, CA, 90631

name: City of Yorba Linda Parks and Recreation Department
orgTypeBasis: A municipal department of the City of Yorba Linda with its own director, superintendent and published staff directory at City Hall.
address: 4845 Casa Loma Ave, Yorba Linda, CA 92886
whyTheyFit: The city's own directory lists ten named recreation staff spread across four separate buildings - the Community Center, the Cultural Arts Center, the Travis Ranch Activity Center and the Thomas Lasorda Jr. Field House - so the annual all-staff appreciation has to gather people who never otherwise share a shift, and a department that already splits itself four ways is comfortable travelling to a neutral fifth room.
buyingWindow: Sep (after summer camp season closes), Nov-Dec (city holiday event)
headcountBasis: Ten named full-time recreation staff running four facilities implies a part-time instructor, camp and facility-attendant bench several times that size; estimate only.
note: Prospect and competitor in one department. Yorba Linda Parks and Recreation sells youth classes and camps, and rents the Thomas Lasorda Jr. Field House and the Community Center for parties and team events - the same spend a group-sales calendar is chasing. The staff-appreciation ask is clean; the youth-programme conversation is not, so do not open with it. The city publishes individual staff emails, which is unusual for this trade area and is the reason this row has a named door rather than a form.
addressSource: City of Yorba Linda staff directory (yorbalindaca.gov/directory.aspx), read 14 August 2026, which gives City Hall as 4845 Casa Loma Avenue, Yorba Linda, CA 92886 and the Parks and Recreation line as 714-961-7160.
matchedAddress: 4845 CASA LOMA AVE, YORBA LINDA, CA, 92886

name: City of Fullerton Human Resources Department
orgTypeBasis: A department of the City of Fullerton at City Hall with its own published department inbox and phone line.
whyTheyFit: Fullerton is the largest single payroll inside the trade area and it still runs its own police department, its own fire department, its own public library and a full parks and recreation operation - and this one department publishes a single inbox that reaches the person who owns the service awards for all of them, which turns four separate pitches into one email 3.7 miles from the venue.
buyingWindow: Nov-Dec (city-wide holiday event and service awards), early May (Public Service Recognition Week)
headcountBasis: A GROUP SIZE, not the payroll. An estimated 500-800 full-time and regular part-time city employees including sworn police and fire, of whom 80-200 would attend any one appreciation night because a city cannot stand down its shifts at once. The adopted budget publishes authorised positions and is the number to confirm on the first call.
note: The competitor sits one block west and belongs to the same city: Fullerton Parks and Recreation runs the Fullerton Community Center at 340 W. Commonwealth, which rents rooms for parties and runs youth programming, and publishes its own inboxes (parks@ci.fullerton.ca.us and FullertonCommunityCenter@ci.fullerton.ca.us). Fullerton is a prospect at 303 and a competitor at 340. Sell the employee side through HR and leave the recreation division alone until there is a referral relationship worth trading.
addressSource: City of Fullerton Human Resources department page (cityoffullerton.com), read 14 August 2026, printing 303 W. Commonwealth Ave., Fullerton, CA 92832.

name: Fullerton Police Department
orgTypeBasis: A city-operated sworn police department with its own headquarters building on Commonwealth and its own recruitment website separate from the city's.
decisionMakerTitle: Recruitment Team Sergeant (ask onward for the Administrative Services Manager)
whyTheyFit: This department runs a standalone recruiting site and a continuous academy pipeline, which means recruit graduations and field-training completions land on the calendar several times a year rather than once - a repeating family occasion at a department a block from City Hall, and one that has to sit midweek because patrol cannot stand down on a Friday.
buyingWindow: Mid-May (National Police Week), academy and field-training graduation dates through the year, Dec
headcountBasis: Sworn plus professional staff for a city of roughly 140,000 running its own department; estimate only, scaled from the city rather than from a published roster.
note: The verified address is the recruitment team's, published on the department's own hiring site - it is a real door but it is a hiring door. Use it to reach a name and then ask for the administrative services side, which owns the department's non-sworn spend. A recruit-graduation family night is a better first ask here than a holiday party, because the date is already fixed by the academy calendar. Phone corrected on audit: the department publishes 714-738-6700 and 714-738-6800 as business lines and 714-738-3377 for recruitment. The number originally recorded appeared on no page that could be loaded.
addressSource: City of Fullerton facility directory entry for the Fullerton Police Department (cityoffullerton.com), read 14 August 2026, printing 237 W. Commonwealth Ave, Fullerton, CA 92832; the same address is printed on the department's own recruitment site joinfullertonpd.com.

name: Yorba Linda Water District
orgTypeBasis: An independent special district with its own elected board and its own administration building, not a city utility department - it publishes its own contact page, mailing address and board agendas.
whyTheyFit: The district keeps its administration building and its field operations yard on the same Miraloma parcel, so office staff and standby crews who never share a working hour share one car park - and the district's single annual employee event is the one evening a year that has to work for both groups at once, which is a booking that needs bowling and a bar rather than a banquet room.
buyingWindow: Dec (holiday event), May (Water Awareness Month and annual safety awards)
headcountBasis: A district serving roughly 80,000 people with its own operations, engineering, finance, IT and customer service functions; estimate only, drawn from service-population scale rather than a published roster.
note: Special districts buy on a board-approved purchase order and publish a monthly check register, so whatever is quoted here appears in a public document with the district's name next to it. Price it so it survives that, and expect the district to want an itemised invoice rather than a package price. The published inbox is a general one - ask it to route to human resources and risk, which is where employee events sit in a district this size.
addressSource: Yorba Linda Water District contact page (ylwd.com/about/contact), read 14 August 2026, printing the office street address as 1717 E. Miraloma Avenue, Placentia, CA 92870-6623.

name: La Habra Heights County Water District
orgTypeBasis: An independent county water district with its own office, its own board minutes and its own billing operation, publishing all of them on its own domain.
address: 1271 N Hacienda Rd, La Habra Heights, CA 90631
whyTheyFit: A district small enough that its published office hours are one line and its whole staff would fit on four lanes - which makes it the opposite of a buyout: a single General Manager can approve a small weekday evening for the office and the field crew without a committee, and it sits four miles up Hacienda from the venue with no comparable venue between.
buyingWindow: Dec (holiday), Jun (fiscal year-end, after the budget is adopted)
headcountBasis: A district serving a single small hillside city with a 7:30am-5:00pm counter and a field crew; estimate only, taken from the size of the service area rather than a published roster.
note: Geocoding note: the district writes its address as 1271 N Hacienda Road and the Census geocoder returned 1271 HACIENDA RD without the directional. Both the N and the S forms of the query return the identical TIGER segment, which means the directional simply is not carried for this road - it is not a match on a different street, so the row is kept as matched rather than flagged. Also note this is Los Angeles County, not Orange, which changes nothing about the drive but changes who its board answers to.
addressSource: La Habra Heights County Water District contact page (lhhcwd.com/contact.html), read 14 August 2026, printing 1271 N Hacienda Road, La Habra Heights, CA 90631 with office hours and phone.
matchedAddress: 1271 HACIENDA RD, LA HABRA HEIGHTS, CA, 90631

name: OC Public Libraries - Brea Branch Library
orgTypeBasis: A County of Orange facility, not a city one - staff sit under OC Community Resources, which is why the branch inbox runs on occr.ocgov.com rather than on the city's domain.
whyTheyFit: A county branch sitting inside Brea's Civic and Cultural Center, closed Sundays and open six days, whose teen volunteers work the summer reading programme through to an August finish - the thank-you for that volunteer corps is a bigger group than the paid staff and it lands in the one month a new venue most needs a weekday afternoon booking.
buyingWindow: Aug (summer reading wrap and teen volunteer thank-you), Dec
headcountBasis: Branch-level staff for a six-day suburban branch, plus the seasonal teen volunteer corps that roughly doubles the room in August; estimate only. County-wide OCPL is far larger but buys regionally, not from a branch.
note: This is the county agency in the trade area, and it happens to share a building with two city prospects already on this list - City of Brea Human Resources and Brea Police Department - so one walk into 1 Civic Center Cir reaches three separate employers with three separate budgets. Three pins legitimately stack on this coordinate.
addressSource: OC Public Libraries Brea branch page (ocpl.org/libraries/brea), read 14 August 2026, printing 1 Civic Center Circle, Brea, CA 92821 with the branch phone, hours and branch inbox.

name: Placentia-Yorba Linda Unified School District - Transportation Department
orgTypeBasis: A school district operating department with its own yard, its own director and an eleven-person office roster published on the district's own site - it buys on a district purchase order.
whyTheyFit: The yard publishes its whole office - a director, a field-trip dispatcher, two special-education dispatchers, two bus driver instructors and a training supervisor - and posts its hours as 6:00am to 4:30pm, which means the only hour this department can be gathered is a weekday late afternoon, the deadest inventory a venue owns and the one it can afford to give away well.
buyingWindow: Late Apr (School Bus Driver Appreciation), Jun (end of school year), Aug (pre-service week before routes restart)
headcountBasis: A district of roughly 24,000 students running general-education and special-education routes plus its own maintenance; drivers, aides, mechanics and dispatch. Estimate only - the office roster is published, the driver roster is not.
note: Worth saying aloud: this row is a prospect and a channel at the same time. The field-trip dispatcher listed on this page is the person who books the coaches for the schools already on this board, so the department that gets thanked here is also the department that has to be phoned before any school can bring a bus to the venue. Get the driver-appreciation night and the field-trip route opens with it.
addressSource: PYLUSD Transportation Department page on the district's own site, read 14 August 2026, printing 1301 E. Orangethorpe Ave. Placentia, CA 92870 with hours and the full staff directory.

name: City of Placentia (City Hall)
orgTypeBasis: A general-law city with its own police department and its own administration; the organisation is unambiguously real, only its pin is not.
whyTheyFit: Placentia is one of the few cities in north Orange County that still runs its own police department alongside a full city payroll, and it sits four miles from the venue with the district transportation yard and the library district on the same few blocks - a single afternoon in Placentia could reach three public payrolls.
buyingWindow: Nov-Dec (city-wide holiday event and service awards), early May (Public Service Recognition Week)
headcountBasis: A city of roughly 52,000 running its own sworn police department plus public works, finance and community services; estimate only, and unverified because no city page would load.
note: Two failures, either of which would be enough on its own. Do not put this row back without a first-party address page and a coordinate that lands on the east side of Chapman.
addressSource: No first-party page was obtainable. placentia.org's staff directory, contact-us and city-hall-info pages all refused automated reading across repeated attempts on 14 August 2026, and the only 401 E Chapman citations found were third-party aggregator listings, which rule 1 says are not enough on their own.
excludeReason: The Census geocoder returned 401 W CHAPMAN AVE, PLACENTIA - the opposite directional, a different segment of the road roughly six-tenths of a mile west of the block the city sits on. It is not a coverage gap: 411 E Chapman, the Placentia Library District a few doors along, matches cleanly on the east side, and TIGER's E Chapman range in Placentia starts at 403, so there is no public address range for 401 on the east side and the only coordinate on offer is the wrong road. That is the same failure that took Round One Entertainment off this board, and it is compounded by the address being single-sourced from aggregators because no City of Placentia page would load.
